Author: CrownedPandaXIV
Name: XIV Fleet Companion
Description:
Got a massive fleet of submarines? Always struggling to see which ones need upgrades? Wanna see your multi-account fleet at a glance? Give this a try!

Subs and their routes, supplies, parts, retainers, Free Companies, inventories, income, the market and trends, all in the game. Keep your fleet on this PC with nothing else to install, or share it between PCs (and with the free Windows app) through a database. Type /xivfleet to start.

Needs:
• AutoRetainer (from https://love.puni.sh/ment.json)

Works best with:
• Allagan Tools: bags, retainers' items and FC chests
• FC Tracker (from https://puni.sh/api/repository/erdelf): FC houses
• Submarine Tracker: voyage loot

Thanks to kawaii, NightmareXIV and the Puni.sh team (AutoRetainer), Critical_Impact (Allagan Tools), erdelf (FC Tracker) and Infi (Submarine Tracker) for their plugins.
Punchline: Here to help manage your EMPIAH!
Changelog:
The Sub Calculator: five new pages for planning sub builds, routes and levelling, under a new Sub Calculator group in the sidebar.

### New: the Sub Calculator

- Voyage Planner, as in the app. Pick a rank, four parts and up to five sectors, or start from one of your subs, and see:
- the build's surveillance, retrieval, speed, range and favor;
- the range the route uses against the sub's, the voyage length, experience and ceruleum, with Best order to put the sectors in the fastest order the sub's range allows;
- for each sector, the loot tier, retrieval and double dip the build reaches (amber where XIVStats and Pepper's guide disagree, with how much more of a stat it needs);
- the loot it can bring back, with how often ("about 1 in 15 voyages") and what one is worth, gil per voyage and per day, experience per day with the bonus the build is sure of (and the most luck can add), and repair kits a day (parts' wear as Submarine Tracker predicts it). With Live Market Prices on, the loot is priced on the market, on a world, data center or region you choose (your sub's data center to start). The plugin's figures are checked against the app's. /xivfleet planner opens it.
- Route Finder, as in the app. Two tabs:
- Best routes: for one of your subs (or any parts and rank), a map, and what to go for (experience, gil or a chosen item), every route of up to five sectors that fits the sub's range and the longest voyage you pick, best first, with the loot tier at each stop and the range to spare. The map's sectors are tiles coloured by what your Free Company has done (explored, explore next, could open by chance, not yet); click one to make it a must, again to leave it out. Only sectors your FC has discovered are used, and routes that explore something new can go first. Gil is at vendor prices.
- Unlocks: what your FC is sure to explore next, what could open by chance and from where, and the way to the next map, step by step. /xivfleet routefinder opens it.
- Build Finder, as in the app. Pick up to five sectors and what you want from each (a loot tier, optimal retrieval, a double dip, or particular items), and see every build that gets it, at the lowest rank its stats and parts allow:
- what the goals need, the rank and the route's range, and each build's stats with what it has to spare (hover a "+" for what it's measured against), its voyage, and the parts you'd still need to get;
- amber where only the lower of XIVStats' and Pepper's figures is met, or only builds sure to reach it;
- sorted by lowest rank (grouped by rank), fastest voyage, fewest parts to get or most range to spare;
- Find an item: every sector on every map that drops it, with the rank it needs, the tier, how often and how many at each retrieval; Add puts it in as a goal;
- Only these parts: a filter per slot (Any, Standard only, Modified only, Ones I own, or parts to tick); a slot's Any is highlighted while it has a filter. The plugin's builds are checked against the app's. /xivfleet buildfinder opens it.
- Compare Builds, as in the app. Up to three builds side by side: one of your subs, one typed in, or Add to compare from the Build Finder and Voyage Planner. Same route compares the builds alone (a build that can't fly it says why); Best route each gives each build its own best route on a map, for experience or gil. Rows: the five stats, range used, voyage, experience and gil a voyage and a day, repair kits, gil after repairs, and what each build reaches at each stop; the best in each row is green. Gil at vendor prices. The plugin's figures are checked against the app's. /xivfleet compare opens it.
- Levelling Plan, as in the app. A sub's way from its rank to a target (its next build's rank to start, else the top rank), each voyage on the route best for experience an hour at its rank, experience carrying over as the game gives it:
- voyages, days and the date it gets there, ceruleum and repair kits, and a strip showing each stage's share;
- the stages as a table: ranks, time, voyages, route (with the sectors a new rank opens), parts, voyage length and experience, and, where a sector your FC hasn't discovered would do at least 1% better, by how much;
- one sub, or every sub in a Free Company (a row each, with its own target);
- keep the build, or suggest part swaps on the way (only parts the sub's rank allows; Standard parts only if you like), each saying whether you have the part and how much sooner it gets there, as a line before the stage that uses it;
- Use every sector: the plan as if every sector were discovered. A plan from rank 1 to 145 takes about a second; changing a choice starts the new plan at once. The working out runs below the game's priority, so the framerate holds. The plugin's plans are checked against the app's. /xivfleet levelling opens it.

### Across the Sub Calculator

- Choosing a sub or a Free Company: a panel grouped by account label (characters and Free Companies in Character Roster order, with their world), with a search.
- Tables like every other page's: columns to size, move, sort and choose.
- Clear buttons on every search and selection: Clear sub, Clear route, Clear marks, Clear goals, Remove all builds, Reset target(s). Each shows only while there's something to clear.
- "Working out…" while a page works out its answer, the old answer dimmed until the new one is in.
- An amber note for a part the rank can't fit yet on the Voyage Planner and Compare Builds ("Not fittable at rank 10 yet: Modified Whale (Hull) needs rank 50."); the build is still worked out as typed.
- The game data behind it: the loot each sector can give, by tier, and the stat breakpoints, from XIVStats with Pepper's FFXIV Ship Guide's beside them, shipped with the plugin and read again at each release. Surveillance, retrieval and favor are read from the game's files alongside speed and range.

### Elsewhere

- Open in Voyage Planner on each row of the Subs and Route Optimization pages.
- Fight Club routes your FC can't run yet are marked on Subs and Route Optimization: "needs R" (hover: where it opens from), with the best Fight Club route the FC can run now below it.
- The next build on the Subs page stops at the game's top rank (145). The game's rank table also lists experience "to the next rank" on the top rank, so the top was taken as 146.
- Market prices skip odd listings (Income, Gil & Market and the Voyage Planner): a lone listing far below the others is skipped, and a price still far under the last week's sales uses those instead. A price changed this way is amber, with a hover saying why; Income lists the items whose prices were changed.
- The repair kit price is set on the Supplies page, beside what to buy, instead of in Settings.
- Sub part condition is recorded. In the Free Company's workshop, the plugin reads each sub part's condition and saves the changes at the next sync, so the Sub Calculator can later work out how much each voyage wears your parts. Nothing shows it yet.
- Explored sub sectors are recorded. In the workshop, once the game has its sub list (the Voyage Control Panel's submarines opened, as AutoRetainer does at each collection), the plugin reads which sectors the FC has unlocked and explored and saves them at the next sync (database update 18). The Route Finder and Levelling Plan use them; until then every sector is allowed and they say "not read yet".
